# Harmonic for Hacker News Harmonic for Hacker News is an Android Hacker News client which is meant to be modern, fast and well thought out. You can find it on Google Play for download. This has been my personal side project since 2020 and since starting my PhD in 2021 the time I have to dedicate to Harmonic has decreased. My personal philosophy on side projects is that the most important thing is building something that is actually shipped. Since much of my knowledge on building Android apps is ~10 years old, Harmonic does not use Kotlin or the latest Android API's and is probably not the easiest app to dig into the source code of. However, it is shipped, and it works fairly well in my opinion at least. :) The purpose of open-sourcing Harmonic is thus mainly to enable interested users to submit pull requests fixing issues or adding features. I would like to still be able to find my way around the app's code so I am not looking for a full Kotlin rewrite but if you have something you'd like to see fixed or added I am very open to PR's. I'll still commit things myself when I have time. # Features * Basic account functionality: log in, vote, comment, and submit * Material 3 design with some nice animations * Several themes including full black * A ton of customization options, bordering on feature creep * Fast!

steps.message: Done. The build succeeds and the bug is fixed. ## Diagnosis The truncation is **not** done by the app or the vendored `HtmlTextView` library — I verified that `HtmlTagHandler` renders anchor text verbatim, and found no `ellipsize`/`substring` logic on the comment body. It comes from **Hacker News' own server-side HTML**, which shortens the *visible* text of long links while keeping the full URL in the `href`: ```html https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/files/monetar... ``` `DialogUtils.showTextSelectionDialog()` passed that raw HTML straight to `setHtml(text)`. So the select-text view inherited HN's truncation — and since selection operates on rendered text, selecting a link could never yield more than the `...`-terminated prefix. The full URL was sitting right there in the `href`, just never rendered. ## Fix Added `Utils.expandTruncatedLinks(String html)`, which rewrites each anchor's inner text with its full `href`, and called it from the select-text dialog. The key design concern was **not clobbering legitimate link text**. A blanket "replace all anchor text with the href" would turn `click here` into a raw URL. So `isTruncatedVersionOf()` only substitutes when the text is genuinely an ellipsized form of its own href — the text ends in `...` (or `…`) *and* the remaining prefix actually prefixes the href. Descriptive text, and prose that merely trails off with `...`, is left alone. Details worth noting: - **Escaped entities**: text and href are compared in their HTML-escaped form. That's sound because both come from the same document and are unescaped identically downstream, so `&` in a query string matches correctly. - **`Matcher.quoteReplacement`**: without it, a `$` or `\` in a URL would corrupt `appendReplacement`. - **Scheme-less display text** is handled, since HN sometimes omits `https://`. - Anything ambiguous falls through and is left untouched — a no-op, never corruption. I validated this against 13 cases in a standalone harness (real HN-style links, descriptive text, prose ellipsis, multiple mixed links per comment, escaped ampersands, `$`/`\` in URLs, unicode ellipsis, null/empty) before building. Two notes on scope: - I deliberately kept the change to the select-text view, matching the report. The adjacent **"copy text"** action in `CommentsFragment` (line 1600) does `Html.fromHtml(comment.text)` and has the *same* underlying defect — copied links are truncated too. It's a one-line reuse of the new helper if you want it fixed, but I left it out rather than widen scope unasked. - The normal comment list still shows HN's truncated links, which I understood to be intended for layout reasons per the report's framing. The patch is saved at `bug-171_fix.patch` (this directory is under the research repo's gitignored `runs/`, so there was no VCS baseline — I reconstructed the originals to produce a proper unified diff).
